items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: I got in Sam's band in 1922.

ctx.x: When did you join Sam Morgan? That was your first job, you said, I believe.
I got in Sam's band in 1922. 22.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: When I was with Sam Morgan, we had eight pieces in our band

ctx.x: You know, when I used to go up to Tyler's Big Auden in 1945, you weren't even here then, but you were in New York, I guess. I had Joe Avery and, and we were coming up there. I never heard a solo the whole time I was there. Not one solo. The trumpet would take down and that was all.

Well, and now, now I see, you're just switching to the truth. Now you take, now you take, but Lewis, Lewis Armstrong would tell you himself. The time that, when he was, when he was playing, when he was playing here. When he was at the Dixieland bands, there's no trumpet tape, no solo bar himself, or a clarinet, or a trombone. Sometimes the music would call for, sometimes three or four bars solo, something like that. Three or four bars. Some others would take it, you see. But now like, you play a solo, I take one,…
Really? What was Howard playing? Yes. Trumpet.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: With Sam's band or...? Yeah, with Sam's band. Me making them records in...

ctx.x: Alright, let's go from there now. See we did one of these before. We were talking about Sam Morgan's band. I wanted to ask you a little bit about making those records.
With Sam's band or...? Yeah, with Sam's band. Me making them records in... ...2024. 1924, huh? 1924. That's where I could... ...where I could get to. 24. 24.
Well, who did you make the records for?

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: And Sam Morgan Band, in the section where I live at, if you get Sam Morgan Band, you're going to draw the people.

ctx.x: Especially the Dixieland jazz. It reaches so many, many people. What about keeping time? Did y'all keep good time there? Did people dance to the bands?

That's what I made in the dance bar, didn't you? When you hit the ball. There ain't no big band. There ain't no big band. There ain't no big band. There ain't no big band. The band didn't play as fast as they're playing. They people called that circus music. But if you were the colored balls, all the white dancers, that's all you had was jazz bands. Now you had good bands now in them times. The band he played was a lot of games of my life. And Sam Morgan Band, in the section where I live at, if you get Sam Morgan…
That's a... They had some dancers from their heart.
